classification: Editorial progression summaries of already-recorded evidence, not new analyst testimony or a fresh earnings sweep.

updates.Micron: The newer exchanges move from supply agreements to their economics: separate contract vintages and price resets, inventory-cost recognition, and construction-to-qualified-output lags. Higher CapEx is not immediate bit supply, and customer deposits are not unrestricted shareholder-return cash.
updates.AMD: The next modeling questions are customer financing and energized sites, HBM cost-recovery timing, and three separate warrant channels: net revenue, potential dilution and noncash remeasurement. Management's Q4 margin benchmark is not a guaranteed 2027 floor; CPU/AI mix remains an open input.
updates.Intel: The latest questions separate PC sell-in recovery from end consumption and test DCAI annualization against wafer/substrate timing and Xeon/ASIC mix. Management accepting an analyst's starting point does not turn that arithmetic into formal annual guidance.
updates.TSMC: Demand-to-capacity translation now explicitly includes customer financing, power, construction and components. Management's demand assessment still needs commissioned-capacity evidence; compare High-NA alternatives by qualified cost per good die, not first-tool installation.
updates.Microsoft: The progression is from buying capacity to obtaining usable output: distinguish shared-fleet efficiency and token pricing from delayed capacity delivery. Cross-product benefits are not automatically additive revenue, and a delivery delay does not guarantee later catch-up.
updates.Alphabet: TPU system sales add an inventory-and-receivables funding bridge before delivery and billing. A change in the CapEx model does not by itself lower total cash intensity, and undisclosed product margins remain a gap.
updates.Amazon: AWS growth now needs a matched-period bridge from commissioned capacity to usage and pricing. Management described uneven additions but did not quantify the sequential driver split; one quarterly growth rate cannot establish a demand turn.
updates.Meta: Main-call questions leave 2027 spending ranges open and separate advertising gains from new AI revenue. The distinct follow-up adds owned-versus-leased capacity, financing permission versus actual issuance, and task-matched compute economics; efficiency is not proof of lower total spending.
updates.Supermicro: The newer questions connect customer advances, delivery-cohort acceptance and liquidity. Separate exceptional delayed-delivery catch-up from routine deferred balances, and cash funded by advances or credit from recurring self-funding. Full-format FY2027 Q1 results remain issuer-labeled preliminary and unaudited, with closing and review incomplete.
updates.Arista: The progression separates scale-up trials from dated revenue adoption, project-specific R&D from recurring spending, and supplier agreements from placed orders and delivered components. Confidence in 2027 supply is not evidence that every order has already been placed.
updates.Eaton: Certification and pilots are distinct from customer adoption; plant-ramp costs need vintage and seasonal comparisons rather than Q4 annualization. Recast the acquisition/disposal perimeter before inferring organic growth or margin improvement; formal 2027 guidance remained deferred.
updates.Schneider Electric: The revenue-update call adds a backlog-to-delivery-cohort question and a prefab installation-speed test. Neither backlog conversion timing nor prefab margin accretion was quantified; faster site installation is not the same as earlier energization or higher supplier margin.
updates.ASML: The latest questions separate contract-vintage pricing effects from immediate margins and test tool output against footprint, cycle time and customers' funded fab readiness. Capacity-reservation behavior remains an alternative explanation for apparent demand.
updates.Lam Research: Supplier constraints move the discussion from visibility to dated shipment and acceptance milestones. Expected March catch-up is not recognized revenue; identify constrained components, funded supplier expansion and qualification before accelerating the model.
updates.Arm: Editorial progression: retain prior history, then separate supply qualification, royalty mix and benchmark comparability. A multi-period silicon target is not an annual cash forecast; average royalty per chip is not a same-product price. Compare matched-generation, matched-workload rack economics before assuming competitive displacement.
updates.Qualcomm: Editorial progression: separate price-realization lag, data-center business mix and segment reclassification. Recast QCT on a comparable perimeter; lower gross margin need not imply lower operating margin. Test Android sell-in against platform-level channel inventory and consumption before calling a recovery.
updates.CoreWeave: Editorial progression: reconcile customer price commitments, supplier purchase orders, energization and financing. Offered capacity is a subset of the pipeline; management clarified 2028 capacity was not yet marketed. Positive adjusted operating profit is not GAAP net profitability.
updates.Digital Realty: Editorial followthrough from selected Q&A: Separate rent growth, construction cost, financing currency and timing before inferring equity returns.
updates.Equinix: Editorial followthrough from selected Q&A: Audit permitting, executed power agreements, energization and ready-for-service separately; modular equipment can reduce schedule risk without eliminating it.
updates.KLA: Editorial followthrough from selected Q&A: Separate customer investment mix, process-control intensity and KLA shipment constraints; demand alone does not determine recognized revenue.
updates.SK hynix: Editorial followthrough from selected Q&A: Track shell readiness, equipment installation, qualified bit output and buyer financing separately; capital spending is not immediate supply.
updates.Samsung: Editorial followthrough from selected Q&A: Normalize spending into physical capacity, yield and timing; a tight-supply forecast is management judgment, not verified future output.
updates.Vertiv: Editorial followthrough from selected Q&A: Reconcile purchase orders, capacity reservations, cancellation rights and shipment timing before using backlog as revenue visibility.
